reviews.comment: HE IS SUCH AN AMAZING PROF!!! He is clearly very passionate about statistics and it's evident in the way he teaches. Participation is very important- he notices when you skip and holds you accountable. Do practice problems and don't hesitate to reach out to him when needed. Math has always been super hard for me but he made the class enjoyable.
Lectures and slides were organized, two multiple choice exams worth 50% of total grade. Class isn't difficult if you follow along in lectures.
The average for the final was a 65, which means a lot of students failed it. It's test heavy, so it dropped my grade by a whole letter grade.

Had him for Stat-211 (wasn't an option to choose). He is a great professor and truly does care about the students. Grades are homework and midterms/final only. The tests are literally the homework. I never went to class after the first midterm and got an A from using his lecture notes. Overall great dude, great teacher.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! ATTEND CLASS. Though attendance not mandatory it is very helpful. If you have time I also recommend attending office hours. He is very helpful and looks out for his students by giving out practice exams and allowing cheat sheets. If you get the chance chose this professor!

I am bad at anything with numbers, but was able to survive with a B. Akinbode was a decent teacher, but if you are not used to listening to accents, I recommend you sit at the front. Go to recitation if you are lost and try to practice the material on your own. My grade is what happens when your require and INTA major to take a math class.
reviews.ratingTags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: don't take this class unless you want to teach yourself every topic before exams because you can't understand a word he says.

He is very nice and definitely wants his students to succeed. He gives reviews for his tests that are basically made from the exam itself. You are allowed cheat sheets on every exam and you can put pretty much whatever on them. He can be a bit hard to understand and can confuse himself at times but I found him to be sufficient to learn the material

Some of the other reviews are giving this guy a bad reputation. Yes he has a heavy accent, but if you sit close, genuinely try to understand his voice and participate the lectures are actually pretty helpful. The content itself is easy and if you attend the in-class review and study those questions there is no reason you shouldn't do well on tests.

I took STAT 303 (won't let me pick it). he's lost man. he doesn't have a clue in the world. This had to have been his first few months on earth because he never used the slides. We would lowkirkenuinely have to do 100 slides in a class to stay on schedule but only get through maybe 20. Then he would just skip the rest

I took him for STAT 201. He was very nice but could be hard to understand at times. He mostly taught by writing on the board instead of going off the slides. The class itself was manageable if you put in the work, and you're allowed a cheat sheet on every quiz and exam. He also gives a lot of practice questions.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy and makes it known that he's there to help outside of class. I couldn't understand him much, so I ended up going to my TA three times a week for help. I put A LOT of effort into this class and got an A, so it is manageable if it's the only available class, but if you can, I'd take someone else.

Best stats 201 prof. Easy hw and unlocked quizzes. IF you want a 80 and above on exams go to class and attend class review sessions. Base your cheat sheet around these SESSIONS there is no way to fail if you do. For an A I would say participate in class, ask questions, and practice his review problems  and after attend his office hours they help!

He is a good person, but when it comes to teaching he is just not a good professor. He has a heavy accent which makes it hard to understand him, as well as his handwriting is not legible at all most of the time. I had to teach myself most of the concepts and struggled a lot.

I have truly taken many professors with heavy accents and he was so difficult to understand. Could not tell you if he was a good professor or not because I could not hear a single word. I played one of his videos for a friend and they also could not understand a single word he said.  He was really understanding with quiz grades though.

There are only 3 tests total and that includes the final, so you need to truly know the content to do well.  He is also hard to understand due to his accent and his handwriting it hard to make out as well.  The concepts he is teaching are not hard if you do the practice problems though.  I dropped because I switched majors, not because of the prof.

Take him. He might not have many reviews but he's good, trust me. He goes over the slides very well and explains everything well. His lectures are engaging and not boring. His test reviews are awesome, if you truly understand his test review there's no way you're getting below a 90 on his exams. Quizzes are done in groups. Super easy class.

Dr. Akinbode is a very fair and caring professor. He makes himself available outside of lecture time and responds very timely to emails. Attendance is required, but lectures are enjoyable. He provides plenty of resources for exams and wants the best for his students. Overall great professor, and if you take stat 201 take Dr. Akinbode.
